subject: ventures/ranked-ballot-counter
professional: an election administrator or returning officer who certifies ranked-choice tabulations (IRV and multi-seat STV) and the club/union secretary who runs one. First checks: does the IRV count use continuing ballots for the majority and exhaust overvotes, does the STV surplus transfer match a published WIGM rule (Scottish Local Government Elections Order 2007, 5-decimal truncation) with every vote accounted for, is the declared winner the one the named method defines, and does a real form export get read without stray columns becoming candidates.

evidence.correctness: Wrote an independent Python IRV / STV (WIGM, transfer value = surplus x paper value / total truncated to 1e-5, as the Scottish SSI 2007/42 order describes) / Schulze (winner set per Schulze 2011: candidates no one beats on strongest paths) in scratchpad rbc/indep.py, with its own random generator, and drove the tool through rbc/run_tool.mjs. Seed 20261122, 3,000 elections: IRV 2,644/2,644 untied winners agree; STV elected sets 2,778/2,778 agree and final exhausted + lost-to-rounding agree to the 1e-5 unit in 2,778/2,778; Condorcet winner 3,000/3,000; Schulze winners 2,981/3,000 (seed 7: 2,987/3,000). Every Schulze mismatch is the tool naming one winner where strongest paths tie: hand-checked profile '20: C2 > C1 / 15: C3 > C1 > C0 / 20: C0 > C2 > C1 > C3' has p[C2,C0] = p[C0,C2] = 35 (C2->C1->C0 = min(40,35); direct C0 over C2 35-20), so Schulze's winner set is {C0, C2}, but the tool reports 'Schulze ranking: C2 > C0 = C1 > C3' and the page shows 'Schulze winner C2', because it ranks by how many candidates each beats. Wikipedia four-city example counted by hand: round 1 M42 N26 C15 K17, C out -> K32, N out -> K58 of 100; tool identical, Schulze N > C > K > M matches the hand pairwise table (C over K 83-17, etc). Wikipedia STV 'food' example (20 ballots, 3 seats, Droop 6) with Wikipedia's names elects Chocolate, Oranges, Strawberries as Wikipedia states. Schulze 45-voter example: my script gives E as sole winner, tool ranks E first. Separately, a realistic form export whose rank headers carry question text ('Your 1st choice') is read with timestamps and e-mail addresses as candidates and the header as a ballot (IRV 'winner: 2026/11/01 10:03:00'). IRV and STV arithmetic are right; the Schulze winner and the CSV misread are wrong outputs, so 2.
evidence.completeness: Claimed features checked end to end via cli.mjs: IRV rounds with eliminations and exhausted counts, STV stages with quota, surplus transfers and lost-to-rounding, Schulze ranking, Condorcet winner, pairwise table, first-preference plurality, warnings (blank, repeat, skip, equal rank, lot), seeded lot reproducible, --json, --csv with formula guard, three input layouts (preference lines, rank columns, Google Forms grid with Timestamp/ID ignored). All work. Gap: one-row-per-ballot CSV with descriptive headers (not parseable as ranks) is not recognised. Guide page numbers all reproduce. No TODOs or stubs.
evidence.verification: node --test '*.test.mjs': 37/37 pass in 0.4 s. crosscheck: node crosscheck/gen.mjs | python3 crosscheck/check.py -> 'IRV: 1909 of 1909 untied elections agree; Schulze full ranking: 3000 of 3000 agree' (the crosscheck copies the same wins-count Schulze ranking, so it cannot see the tie defect). Seeded 7 mutants with quality_mutate.py: 4 SURVIVED (STV quota test >= -> >; tie-break looks at earliest instead of most recent round; IRV majority of all ballots instead of live ballots, though a test is named for exactly that; Schulze wins counted with >= instead of >), 3 caught (exhaust-stays-exhausted removed, equal ranking counted for first, Math.floor -> Math.round in transfer). No STV test against another program.
evidence.craft: Read ballots.mjs (483 lines), cli.mjs, index.html script, usage.mjs, tests. One pure zero-dependency engine shared by page and CLI; integer vote units avoid float drift; output escaped (esc at index.html:159); CSV formula guard; storage wrapped. Defects: the names-in-order fallback (ballots.mjs:150-151) reads every column, META ones included, and keeps the header as a ballot unless every header cell is a rank or META word; the STV election snapshot lists reached-but-unseated candidates in 'elected' (ballots.mjs:313); Schulze ordering by win count rather than the strongest-path relation (ballots.mjs:395-401).
evidence.claims: Backed: 'nothing uploaded' (page.test.mjs network assertion, no fetch/XHR in index.html or usage.mjs); DNT and GPC honoured (usage.mjs:34, usage.test.mjs); disclaimer and not-for-public-elections on page, guide and README; Wikipedia four-city and Schulze examples (tests and my recount); crosscheck 3,000 elections (re-run, numbers identical). Not backed: README.md:36 'Columns named Timestamp, Email address, ID and similar are never read as candidates' (false for the names-in-order layout, shown above); index.html:105 'a candidate ranks above another when its strongest path to them is stronger than theirs back' (the code ranks by count of wins, putting C2 above C0 at equal strongest paths); README.md:80 '36 tests' (37 now); llms.txt:5 '3,000 elections, all agreeing' (IRV agreed on the 1,909 untied ones). served-copy.mjs: no placeholder or retired origin left.
evidence.fitness: Walked the job of a club secretary: a Google Form with one dropdown per rank, exported as CSV. If the questions are titled '1st choice', '2nd choice' the count is right; titled 'Your 1st choice' (or 'Favourite', 'Second favourite') the tool reads 16 candidates including timestamps and e-mail addresses and elects a timestamp, with no warning pointing at the header. The FAQ-recommended multiple-choice grid works, as do pasted preference lines. The garbage is visible, so a user would not certify it, but they cannot finish the job without re-titling columns, and nothing tells them to. Multi-seat STV and IRV counts with every round shown are what a committee needs.
evidence.domain: IRV: majority of continuing ballots, single elimination, overvote at the next live rank exhausts and stays exhausted: in line with Minneapolis/Maine-style rules; departures: an equal ranking whose other candidates are already eliminated counts for the survivor (statutes usually exhaust at the overvote regardless) and skipped ranks always close up (Maine exhausts after two consecutive skips). STV: Droop quota, WIGM with 5-decimal truncation, largest surplus first, last hopefuls deemed elected: matches the Scottish 2007 order's arithmetic; departure: an excluded candidate's papers move in one step, not in sub-transfers by value with an election check after each (Scottish rule). Tie-break by most recent differing round then lot is a recognised practice. All framed as 'not any statute'. Schulze ranking/winner departs from Schulze 2011 when strongest paths tie (above).

const c = dead[i] ? -1 : nextChoice(b.ranking, live); -> const c = nextChoice(b.ranking, live);

defects.what: Schulze winner and ranking come from counting how many candidates each beats on strongest paths, not from the strongest-path relation: when two candidates' strongest paths tie, the tool names one Schulze winner (page 'Schulze winner C2') where Schulze 2011 gives a tie {C0, C2}. 19 of 3,000 random elections (13 of 3,000 on another seed). The author's crosscheck/check.py copies the same rule, so it agreed.

One-row-per-ballot CSV whose headers are not parseable as ranks ('Your 1st choice', 'Favourite') falls to the names-in-order layout, which reads every column (Timestamp, e-mail) as candidates and counts the header row as a ballot, with no warning; IRV 'elects' a timestamp.
README says Timestamp, Email address, ID columns are never read as candidates; false in the names-in-order layout.
Page says Schulze ranks a candidate above another when its strongest path to them is stronger; code ranks by number of wins, so it ranks above at equal strongest paths.

Four of seven seeded mutants in core counting survive: STV 'at or over quota' boundary, tie-break look-back direction, IRV majority of live vs all ballots (the test named for this rule passes under either), Schulze strict win count.
STV election snapshot's 'elected' list includes candidates that reached quota but were not seated because seats ran out; the action text's verb agreement also uses reached.length.

Exclusion moves all of a candidate's papers in one step; the Scottish WIGM order the comments cite transfers by value in sub-stages with an election check after each, which can change who is elected in rare cases. Disclosed only generally ('not any statute').
README verification says 36 tests; the suite has 37.
llms.txt says the Python recount of 3,000 elections was 'all agreeing'; IRV agreement was on the 1,909 untied elections only.

verdict: IRV and multi-seat STV are counted correctly: an independently written Python IRV and Scottish-style WIGM agree on every untied winner (2,644/2,644) and every STV elected set with exhausted and rounding residue exact to 1e-5 (2,778/2,778), and the Wikipedia four-city and STV food examples count to their published results. Two faults keep it below the bar. The Schulze winner is derived from win counts, so in tied strongest-path profiles (about 0.5% of random elections; e.g. '20: C2 > C1 / 15: C3 > C1 > C0 / 20: C0 > C2 > C1 > C3') it names a single winner where Schulze's own definition gives a tie, contradicting the page's description. And a common Google Forms export with question-text rank headers is read with timestamps and e-mail addresses as candidates, contrary to the README. Four of seven seeded mutants survive. Correctness 2, claims 2, verification 2: does not meet the bar; finished (completeness 3).
